svg.title: Compare the approximation error after checking both strict conditions
svg.desc: The left panel shows X binomial with one hundred trials and probability zero point one, so expected successes ten and failures ninety both exceed five. Its matched normal has mean ten and variance nine. The exact binomial probability of at most ten rounds to 0.5832, while the normal area below ten point five is 0.5662. The absolute difference is 0.0170. The right panel uses probability zero point zero two, giving expected successes two and failures ninety-eight. This fails the strict success-count condition. Its matched normal, mean two and variance one point nine six, is shown only to inspect the mismatch. The exact binomial probability of at most two rounds to 0.6767, while the comparison normal area below two point five is 0.6395, with absolute difference 0.0372. Bars are binomial probability masses and curves are normal densities. The normal curves extend beyond the finite count support, including some negative area; they are not truncated or renormalised. Passing the syllabus conditions does not guarantee a stated number of matching decimal places.
